confirmedFindings.summary: emitHuman re-sorts armedEffectiveDates with Array#sort's default (string) comparator on Date objects, so the ACT BEFORE header can name a later date than the true earliest armed downgrade.
confirmedFindings.detail: Verified against the compose DB: TenantSubscription.downgradeEffectiveAt is `timestamp without time zone`, and node-postgres parses it to a JS Date (constructor Date confirmed). Line 609-611 correctly sorts armedEffectiveDates with a numeric comparator, but line 859 does `[...b216.armedEffectiveDates].sort()[0]`, which compares String(Date) — i.e. it orders by WEEKDAY NAME. Verified counterexample run in node: `[Tue Sep 01 2026, Thu Sep 03 2026].sort()[0]` returns Thu Sep 03 2026. So with two or more armedAfterReinstatement tenants (e.g. effective dates Tue 2026-09-01 and Thu 2026-09-03), the human report prints `ACT BEFORE Thu Sep 03 2026 …` and the owner misses the 2026-09-01 downgrade — the exact money outcome the build plan's Risks table calls out ("one more plan flip + MRR delta per tenant at 02:00") and prints FIRST for that reason. The fixture cannot see this: only tenant B is armedAfterReinstatement, so armedEffectiveDates has length 1 and the bad sort is a no-op in T10/T13. Secondary: the value is interpolated as a raw Date, so the line prints a machine-locale/timezone string ("Tue Sep 01 2026 00:00:00 GMT-0500 (Central Daylight Time)") instead of an ISO date.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Drop the re-sort — use `b216.armedEffectiveDates[0]` (already chronologically sorted at lines 609-611) — and print it as `new Date(x).toISOString()`. Add a second armed-after-reinstatement tenant to the DB spec whose effective date is chronologically earlier but alphabetically later by weekday, and assert the ACT BEFORE line names it.

confirmedFindings.summary: B215's window CTE is unfiltered and lags three snapshot JSON columns over the entire OrderRevision table, so --tenant does not reduce its work and a prod run can hit the 45s statement_timeout and lose the whole report.
confirmedFindings.detail: The `revs` CTE (lines 398-408) computes LAG over `"OrderRevision"` with NO WHERE clause, carrying `r.snapshot`, `LAG(r.snapshot)` and `LAG(r.snapshot, 2)`; every predicate, including `${tenantClause()}`, is applied only in the outer query (lines 411-414). EXPLAIN of that exact SQL against the compose DB proves the tenant predicate is NOT pushed into the CTE (it cannot be — tenantId is not in the window's `PARTITION BY r."orderId"` key): `Subquery Scan on revs  Filter: (… revs."tenantId" = ANY (…) …) -> WindowAgg -> Sort (Sort Key: r."orderId", r."revisionNumber") -> Seq Scan on "OrderRevision" r`. On prod that means a full seq scan of OrderRevision plus a sort of the whole table with three copies of each row's `snapshot` jsonb in the tuple, before a single row is discarded. If it exceeds `SET statement_timeout = '45s'` (line 899) the query rejects, main() rejects, and the process exits 1 having printed nothing — B215 is the 4th of seven sequential sections in main() (lines 903-911), so the already-computed B134/B135/B214 results are thrown away too and the owner gets no report at all. This also defeats the mitigation the build plan states for its own risk row: "The window query returns candidate pairs only. Snapshots load per candidate. The owner can scope with --tenant" — the implementation does neither.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Move the filters into the CTE: `FROM "OrderRevision" r WHERE r.source = 'EDIT' AND r."editedById" IS NOT NULL ${tenantClause("r")}` (tenantClause already accepts an alias), and drop `snapshot`/`LAG(snapshot)`/`LAG(snapshot,2)` from the window so it returns only candidate `(orderId, revisionNumber, prevRevisionNumber)` triples; then load the three snapshots per candidate in a second query keyed on those ids, as the plan describes. Re-run the DB lane — T9's expected values (confirmedPairs=1/O215a, unconfirmablePairs=1/O215d) must be unchanged.

confirmedFindings.summary: The human report prints no monetary amount at all and omits four fields the build-plan section table lists as labelled buckets (spendableRemaining, expiredRemaining, recurringInvoicesEmailed, earliestKeyedOrderAt).
confirmedFindings.detail: emitHuman prints one line per entry of `report.labels[sec]` (lines 869-871), and the labels maps carry only the count buckets. Confirmed by running human mode against the compose DB in this session: the output contains no candidateTotal, spendableRemaining, expiredRemaining, mrrDeltaSum, seatsFreedNear, recurringInvoicesEmailed, buyerPaymentRequestAmount, earliestKeyedOrderAt or armedEffectiveDates line — not one money figure appears anywhere in the report the owner is meant to read to decide whether repairs are needed. build-plan.md's section table lists `spendable, spendableRemaining → UPPER_BOUND`, `expired, expiredRemaining → CONTEXT`, `keyedOrders, earliestKeyedOrderAt → CONTEXT` and `recurringInvoices (+recurringInvoiceIds), recurringInvoicesEmailed → LOWER_BOUND` — those four are outside the `(+…)` parentheses the table uses for id arrays, i.e. labelled buckets — while R4 requires each bucket's label "in both human and JSON output" and acceptance criterion 3 requires the human run to print "every bucket label". Impact is limited because the amounts are all present in the --json document and per-row in the JSONL (B214 findings carry `remaining`), so nothing is lost, only unreadable from the console summary.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Add `spendableRemaining`/`expiredRemaining` (B214), `recurringInvoicesEmailed` (B131) and `earliestKeyedOrderAt` (B215) to their sections' `labels` maps — emitHuman then prints them automatically with the right label — and consider one explicit money line per section for candidateTotal, mrrDeltaSum and buyerPaymentRequestAmount. Existing label assertions in T6-T12 check specific keys, not exhaustiveness, so they stay green.

confirmedFindings.summary: B135's only near-miss mutation (DM135B) is excluded by two predicates at once, so neither `dm.type IN ('ADD_ON','REFUSED')` nor the 20-second upper edge of the window is pinned by T7.
confirmedFindings.detail: DM135B is seeded as type DELIVERED **and** at `DONE + 1 s`, which is before CR135A's `resolvedAt` (`DONE + 10 min`) — so it fails the type filter and the `dm."createdAt" >= lm."resolvedAt"` lower bound independently. Traced through the script's LEFT JOIN (lines 249-254): remove `AND dm.type IN ('ADD_ON','REFUSED')` and mutationIds is still `[DM135A]` (DM135B is outside the window), so T7 stays green; widen `+ interval '20 seconds'` to any larger interval and mutationIds is still `[DM135A]` (nothing is seeded between +20 s and later), so T7 stays green again. Only the lower bound is actually pinned (dropping `>=` would pull DM135B in and turn T7 red). A near-miss that fails two predicates at once proves neither — the type filter and the window's upper edge are asserted by nothing.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Seed two more DeliveryMutations on O135/RS1 that must stay out of mutationIds: one DELIVERED at `at(DONE, 10*MIN + 3*SEC)` (inside the window, wrong type — pins the type filter) and one ADD_ON at `at(DONE, 10*MIN + 25*SEC)` (right type, outside the 20 s window — pins the upper edge). T7's `expect(s.mutationIds).toEqual([DM135A_ID])` then goes red if either predicate is loosened.

plan.note: Round 1 fixes all six findings in a single wave (five of them touch report-train4-damage.mjs and/or train4-damage-report.db.spec.ts, so the engine serializes them by file). Script changes: the ACT BEFORE line drops the string-comparator re-sort and prints the chronologically first armed date as ISO (#0); fetchB215 pushes only the tenant filter into the window CTE, strips the three jsonb snapshot columns from the sort tuple in favour of LAG(id)/LAG(id,2), and loads snapshots per candidate in a second read-only query — deliberately NOT moving the source/editedById predicates into the CTE, which would change LAG semantics (#1); the four plan-listed labelled buckets are added to the labels maps and a per-section amounts line prints candidateTotal/mrrDeltaSum/buyerPaymentRequestAmount (#2). Test changes: a fifth armed tenant with a weekday-later-but-earlier date pins the ACT BEFORE ordering; an O215e non-EDIT-between-EDITs near-miss pins the B215 semantics; DM135C/DM135D single-predicate near-misses pin B135's type filter and 20 s upper edge; T4/T5/T8/T14 are strengthened so each fails on its own oracle and a no-op stub cannot pass T14 (#3, #5). The build-plan path typo is a mechanical edit (#4). Expected values from the plan (confirmedPairs=1/O215a, unconfirmablePairs=1/O215d, orphaned=2, spendableRemaining=40, mrrDeltaSum=-50, etc.) must all stay unchanged; tenants moves 4->5 and armedAfterReinstatement 1->2 as a direct consequence of the #0 fixture.

fixed: [#0] emitHuman's ACT BEFORE header no longer re-sorts armedEffectiveDates with Array#sort's default (string) comparator - it takes armedEffectiveDates[0] (already numerically sorted in fetchB216) and prints it via a new formatBucketValue() as an ISO timestamp. DB spec gained a FIFTH fixture tenant E (qa-damage-<sfx>-e / -tenant-e, added to TENANT_IDS/TENANT_SLUGS so scoping+teardown+leak-scan cover it) with only a Tenant row, one armed TenantSubscription and two BillingEvents; its downgradeEffectiveAt is a TUESDAY two days BEFORE tenant B's THURSDAY (both at 12:00 local so the weekday survives the timestamp-without-time-zone read-back skew), i.e. chronologically first but string-sorted last. T10 now asserts armedAfterReinstatement=2, 2 ordinals, armedEffectiveDates=[E,B], that a defaulted sort would name B, and that human stdout contains `ACT BEFORE <E ISO>` and NOT `<B ISO>`. T13 tenants 4->5. DEVIATION FROM DESIGN (evidence-backed): the design said assert armedEffectiveDates[0] === the new tenant's JS Date .toISOString(); I measured against the compose DB that Prisma writes the UTC wall clock into `timestamp without time zone` and node-postgres reads it back as LOCAL time (wrote 2026-09-20T17:00:00.000Z, read back 2026-09-20T22:00:00.000Z, sameInstant:false), so the in-memory Date is NOT the value the script sees; the expected ISO is therefore read back from the DB with the spec's own pool in beforeAll (armedIsoB/armedIsoE) - an oracle independent of the script under test.

[#1] fetchB215's window CTE no longer lags jsonb over the whole OrderRevision table and now honours --tenant. The CTE keeps only ids (LAG(r.id) / LAG(r.id,2) as prevId/prevPrevId; snapshot, LAG(snapshot) and LAG(snapshot,2) removed) and filters `WHERE TRUE ${tenantClause("r")}`; the source/editedById/120s predicates stay in the outer query so LAG still sees the immediately preceding revision whatever its source. A second query through the same `q` helper (`SELECT id, snapshot FROM "OrderRevision" WHERE id = ANY($1::text[])`) loads the de-duplicated candidate snapshots into a Map and assigns curSnapshot/prevSnapshot/prevPrevSnapshot; the bucket loop and findings shape are byte-identical. EXPLAIN against the compose DB now shows `Seq Scan on "OrderRevision" r  Filter: ("tenantId" = ANY (...))` INSIDE the CTE (previously the filter sat only on the outer Subquery Scan). DB spec gained near-miss order O215f (named O215f because O215e was already taken by a different near-miss): r1 EDIT qty 4, r2 source CHANGE_REQUEST qty 5 (+20s), r3 EDIT qty 6 (+40s), same editor - the revision() helper took an optional `source` param. T9 asserts O215f appears in neither id list, with confirmedPairs=1/[O215a], unconfirmablePairs=1/[O215d], keyedOrders=1 unchanged.

[#2] The human report now prints every labelled bucket and every monetary total. Added labels: B214 spendableRemaining=UPPER_BOUND, expiredRemaining=CONTEXT; B131 recurringInvoicesEmailed=LOWER_BOUND; B215 earliestKeyedOrderAt=CONTEXT (JSON section values unchanged). emitHuman's labels loop formats values through formatBucketValue (Date/ISO-looking string -> ISO, null -> "(none)", numbers as before), and a new MONEY_FIELDS map {B134:[candidateTotal], B216:[mrrDeltaSum], B141:[buyerPaymentRequestAmount]} prints `amounts: <field>=<value>` right after it. The id-listing loop, byTenant line and CANNOT_DECIDE prose are untouched (extra label keys match no findings and are skipped). T8 now pins the two new B214 labels; T13 pins /spendableRemaining: 40\s+\[UPPER_BOUND\]/, /expiredRemaining: 5\s+\[CONTEXT\]/, /recurringInvoicesEmailed: \d+\s+\[LOWER_BOUND\]/, /earliestKeyedOrderAt: .*\[CONTEXT\]/, /candidateTotal=100/, /mrrDeltaSum=-50/, /buyerPaymentRequestAmount=12\.5/.
B135's only near-miss mutation (DM135B) is excluded by two predicates at once, so neither `dm.type IN ('ADD_ON','REFUSED')` nor the 20-second upper edge of the window is pinned by T7.
File path is incomplete; the guard file actually exists in a subdirectory

Red gate never went properly RED — the new tests are not proven able to fail (finding [#0]): implemented Fable's design exactly — T8 compares creditNoteIds order-insensitively; T14 now parses the JSON stdout of the run its snapshot pair measured and pins sections.B214.orphaned === 2 plus tenants === 5, so a stub that exits 0 with well-formed JSON fails T14 itself (mutation-probed: stub gave `Expected: 2, Received: 0` at spec line 1357); T4 asserts the script's own literal `Unknown flag: --execute` on stderr FIRST (negative control: a MODULE_NOT_FOUND run exits 1 with stderr not containing that literal); T5 puts status===1 and /No usable connection string/ before the `Cannot find module` guard. T1/T2/T3 source pins and T13's leak scan left unchanged; the script was not touched.

Wave 2 (after the spec edits, since its test also lands in that file) rescopes the B215 LAG window's CTE by the ORDER's tenant instead of the nullable OrderRevision.tenantId, keeps the unscoped case free of the extra semi-join and keeps the outer candidate filter unchanged, with a NULL-middle-revision seed that is red on the current code. Wave 3 clears the check-types gate as an environment fix (build packages/pricing, then npm ci if needed) with an explicit ban on stubs or tsconfig edits; the 45 TS2307 errors sit in files this diff never touched.

fixed: The two new B135 near-misses pin the mutation type filter and the window's 20-second upper edge, but nothing pins its lower edge: removing `dm."createdAt" >= lm."resolvedAt"` leaves all nine DB tests green.

T10's fixture-discriminating assertion (`[E,B].sort()[0]` must be B) depends on the machine's UTC offset being under +12, so the DB lane goes red on a UTC+13/+14 host for a reason that is not a product defect.

The fix for the B215 window pushed the tenant predicate INSIDE the LAG window CTE, but OrderRevision.tenantId is nullable — so under --tenant a NULL-tenant revision is dropped from the window and LAG pairs non-adjacent revisions, both inventing and losing double-fold candidates.
